newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian bourse ends firmer, players eye more data.
newsitem.headline: Belgian bourse ends firmer, players eye more data.

text.p: Belgian shares closed on a higher note on Thursday, helped by low bond market yields, with traders now expecting the market to consolidate until next week as investors await more data to push stocks higher.
"We are fully in a consolidation phase and if there is no bad news concerning bond yields, with the dollar stable, we could see the market higher in a couple of days' time," said one trader.
The blue-chip Bel-20 index closed up 0.30 percent, or 6.07 points, at 2,063.60, with a moderate 2.9 billion francs worth of Belgian shares changing hands.
Dealers said investors were closely following movements in the U.S. markets for direction.

U.S. January employment data, which is due out on Friday, could increase the chances of a Federal Reserve interest rate hike next month and so trigger a slide in bond and share markets if the data is stronger-than-expected.
Investors would continue eyeing the Dow Jones, which plunged 86 points on Wednesday, and was down in early Thursday trade.
Belgian corporate results which got off to a start earlier this week would also give investors direction in coming weeks.

Chemical and drug group UCB, which closed up 0.32 percent at 94,750 francs, announced a pre-tax profit for 1996 up 30 percent to 5.5 billion francs on Wednesday, at the top end of analysts' forecasts, and predicted more growth to come.
"UCB will probably hold at these levels and then gradually rise (more) - it could hit 100,000 quite soon," said trader Paul de Lophem at brokerage Mignon, Hanart, Declerck.
Chemical firm Solvay released earnings after the market closed, saying 1996 group net profit was 13.6 billion francs versus 12.5 billion the previous year.
Solvay closed up 0.34 percent at 22,375 francs.
Elsewhere financials saw the highest rises in the Bel-20, with Generale Bank up 2.3 percent at 12,225 francs helped by a strong dollar and low bond yields.
Kredietbank was another gainer, closing up 1.11 percent at 11,425 francs.
Non-ferrous metals producer Union Miniere gained 1.01 percent to 2,510 francs, boosted by firm zinc price.
